entries.title: Exact dimensional arithmetic
entries.signature: Typed quantity expression -> exact rational quantity or Boolean
entries.domain: Supported scalar time, frequency, voltage, current, power and byte-based memory dimensions; bounded compound units.
preconditions: A valid ordered typed model with compatible dimensions.
Every referenced scalar needed for numerical evaluation has a value.
Denominators are nonzero; integer domains and declared bounds hold.
entries.guarantee: The existing evaluator uses rational arithmetic for the declared inputs. Decimal rendering may be approximate.
non_guarantees: A model value is not an independently measured fact.
Only the shipped unit vocabulary is supported; this is not a complete SI implementation.
entries.cost: At most 16 variables, 128 nodes, depth 24; arithmetic size bounded at 2048 bits.
entries.counterexample: Adding a voltage to a current is invalid even when both numbers are known.
entries.licence: Ledger adapter: existing project source licences. Dependency licences are not independently reviewed by this Atlas; retained distribution notices remain authoritative.

entries.title: Additive interval capacity
entries.signature: Capacity<Q>, allocations<(Q, half-open Time interval)> -> peak demand
entries.domain: A constant nonnegative additive resource capacity and explicit lifetimes.
preconditions: Quantities use compatible dimensions and are nonnegative.
Every interval has known nonnegative times, start < stop, and time units.
Owner explicitly declares additive consumption, fixed capacity and half-open intervals.
No unmodeled overhead, fragmentation or indivisibility.
entries.guarantee: The existing exact event sweep compares the peak of the declared additive model with its fixed capacity.
non_guarantees: No allocator fragmentation, power-rail dynamics or thermal dynamics proof.
A learned method still needs its accepted version and current qualifying evidence at methods.preview.
entries.cost: At most 32 allocations. Event ordering costs O(n log n); emitted active sets can require O(n squared) output.
entries.counterexample: Adjacent half-open intervals need not overlap; closed intervals or allocator overhead need a different profile.
references: Local authority: workbench/schedule_math.py:evaluate; workbench/checked_methods.py:EXPECTED and mapping

entries.title: Linear equality solving
entries.signature: Affine equalities over declared real/integer scalars -> checked assignments or unresolved result
entries.domain: Bounded linear equations with exact rational coefficients.
preconditions: Typed dimensional IR is valid and affine.
At least one equality; inequalities use the feasibility profile.
Pinned SymPy 1.14.0 and mpmath 1.3.0 are required for execution.
entries.guarantee: The existing adapter asks linsolve for a solution and rechecks rational assignments against the original model.
non_guarantees: Admission does not prove consistency, uniqueness or existence.
Underdetermined results remain UNKNOWN in this adapter; resource limits may prevent a result.
entries.cost: At most 16 variables and 32 constraints. Worker limits: 3 CPU seconds, 512 MiB, up to 5 seconds wall time.
entries.counterexample: x + y = 1 does not determine a unique pair; an inequality is not an equality.
entries.licence: Ledger adapter: existing project source licences. Dependency licences are not independently reviewed by this Atlas; retained distribution notices remain authoritative.

entries.title: Linear real and integer feasibility
entries.signature: Affine constraints with real/integer domains -> one witness, infeasible or unknown
entries.domain: The local QF_LIRA-style adapter; not the full capabilities of upstream Z3.
preconditions: Valid typed IR with affine arithmetic and constant nonzero denominators.
Only the local real/integer domains and supported relation nodes.
Pinned z3-solver 4.15.4.0 is required for execution.
entries.guarantee: A returned feasible witness is independently rechecked by the exact IR evaluator.
non_guarantees: A witness is not an optimum or a universal guarantee.
Nonlinear products are refused by this adapter even if upstream Z3 can handle other fragments.
entries.cost: At most 16 variables and 32 constraints; mixed integer solving can be costly. Fixed worker limits, timeout and UNKNOWN are preserved.
entries.counterexample: x*x > 1 is nonlinear; a feasible low-cost candidate does not prove minimum cost.
references: Microsoft Z3 Guide, Arithmetic (live guide consulted 2026-11-02; executable pin is separately 4.15.4.0): https://microsoft.github.io/z3guide/docs/theories/Arithmetic/

entries.title: Rational expression normalization
entries.signature: Supported rational quantity expression -> symbolic form with original domain guards
entries.domain: The bounded rational expression vocabulary of the local SymPy adapter.
preconditions: A valid typed quantity expression, with no constraints selected.
Original denominator restrictions remain attached after cancellation.
Pinned SymPy 1.14.0 and mpmath 1.3.0 are required for execution.
entries.guarantee: The adapter normalizes quantity outputs using cancel and retains original domain conditions.
non_guarantees: x/x becoming 1 does not make x=0 admissible.
Free quantities can leave the numerical state UNKNOWN even when a symbolic form is returned.
entries.cost: Typed model limits apply; fixed 3 CPU seconds / 512 MiB worker budget.
entries.counterexample: Cancelling x/x must not erase the original x != 0 requirement.

entries.title: Declared dependency impact
entries.signature: Finite acyclic reason graph and node -> tracked affected nodes
entries.domain: Explicit proposed dependencies inside a bounded graph.
preconditions: Unique declared nodes and valid edges.
Acyclic dependency structure and a declared starting node.
Coverage outside the supplied graph stays unknown.
entries.guarantee: The existing reasons.impact operation follows tracked dependencies of a saved owned graph.
non_guarantees: A missing edge cannot establish no impact.
Dependencies do not establish causal truth or rule correctness.
entries.cost: Local graph bounds: 64 nodes, 128 rules, 8 premises per rule; topological traversal with bounded sorting.
entries.counterexample: An untracked component can still affect the real project; a cycle is outside this DAG profile.

entries.title: Finite support and refutation paths

preconditions: A valid acyclic finite graph with explicit assumptions.

Rule labels remain proposed interpretations.

non_guarantees: A supported proposed rule is not an independently approved theorem.
Admission validates graph shape only; it does not read or attest arbitrary receipt IDs.
entries.cost: 64 nodes / 128 rules; at most 4096 combinations per expansion and 256 paths per node; budget excess is refused.
entries.counterexample: Two contradictory current observations produce conflict, not permission to choose the preferred result.
